cited_evidence.text: Mechanical properties of single-phase high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be unusually enhanced than many conventional single-phase engineering alloys (). Recent computational and experimental studies indicate that the atomic distribution in such solid solution HEAs may not be completely random as originally believed, but exhibit localized pockets of nonrandom distributions, also called “clustered ordering” (). While strengthening due to such local chemical clusters has been reported in Al (), Ni (), Fe () base alloys, and more recently, in complex bulk metallic glasses () and HEAs (, ), the ability to systematically engineer its nature and extent has so far eluded us. While the quinary CoCrFeNiMn, arguably the most extensively studied HEA, has been established as a single-phase alloy (), local chemical ordering was recently experimentally shown, and computationally validated, in its “subset” ternary CoCrNi alloy (, ) Similarly, direct experimental evidence of nonrandom atomic distributions has been presented in CoCrFeNiPd () and CoNiV () HEAs. In 2014, the first superconducting high-entropy alloy Ta0.34Nb0.33Hf0.08Zr0.14Ti0.11 (in at.%) was discovered []. According to Sun and Cava [], this alloy can be classified as a type-A HEA superconductor. HEAs of this type contain only metals on the left side of the transition metal region of the periodic table, crystallize in a body-centered cubic (bcc) lattice, and exhibit superconducting transition temperatures (Tc) between 4.0 and 9.2 K, while their highest upper critical field (μ0Hc2) is close to 12 T [,,,,,,]. These are the most widely studied HEA superconductors to date. However, it should be noted that most of these alloys contain a large amount of niobium and tantalum, while the titanium concentration is typically less than 20 at.%. Because binary Nb-Ti alloys exhibit much better superconducting properties than Nb-Ta [], it is plausible to expect that NbTi-based high-entropy alloys will have a higher Tc and/or μ0Hc2 compared to previously reported type-A HEA superconductors. Moreover, in the case of various ternary Nb-Ti-Hf and Nb-Ti-Ta and quaternary Nb-Ti-Ta-Hf alloys, the highest values of μ0Hc2 were observed for the titanium-rich alloys [].
